title.en: HTTP vs HTTPS, firewalls and cookies
title.kn: HTTP ಮತ್ತು HTTPS, ಫೈರ್‌ವಾಲ್ ಮತ್ತು ಕುಕೀಗಳು

hook.en: A postcard can be read by every postman who handles it; a sealed envelope cannot. HTTP is the postcard of the web, HTTPS the sealed envelope.
hook.kn: ಅಂಚೆ ಕಾರ್ಡ್ ಅನ್ನು ಅದನ್ನು ಹಿಡಿಯುವ ಪ್ರತಿ ಅಂಚೆಯವನೂ ಓದಬಹುದು; ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಲಕೋಟೆಯನ್ನು ಅಲ್ಲ. HTTP ವೆಬ್‌ನ ಅಂಚೆ ಕಾರ್ಡ್, HTTPS ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಲಕೋಟೆ.

objectives.en: Explain cookies and their privacy risks

narration.en: A postcard can be read by every postman who handles it; a sealed envelope cannot. HTTP is the postcard of the web, HTTPS the sealed envelope.
narration.kn: ಅಂಚೆ ಕಾರ್ಡ್ ಅನ್ನು ಅದನ್ನು ಹಿಡಿಯುವ ಪ್ರತಿ ಅಂಚೆಯವನೂ ಓದಬಹುದು; ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಲಕೋಟೆಯನ್ನು ಅಲ್ಲ. HTTP ವೆಬ್‌ನ ಅಂಚೆ ಕಾರ್ಡ್, HTTPS ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಲಕೋಟೆ.

body.en: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) carries web pages between a browser and a web server as plain text, so anyone who intercepts the traffic can read it. HTTPS (HTTP Secure) sends the same data encrypted using SSL/TLS, so an interceptor sees only scrambled data; the browser shows a padlock and the address begins with https://. Websites that handle logins, payments or personal data should always use HTTPS. HTTPS protects data in transit; it does not guarantee that the website itself is honest or malware-free.

points.en: HTTP: plain text, readable if intercepted
HTTPS: encrypted with SSL/TLS, padlock icon
Use HTTPS for logins and payments

narration.kn: HTTP ದತ್ತಾಂಶವನ್ನು ಸಾದಾ ಪಠ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಕಳುಹಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; HTTPS ಅದನ್ನು SSL/TLS ಮೂಲಕ ಗೂಢಲಿಪೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಲಾಗಿನ್, ಪಾವತಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ HTTPS ಬೇಕು.

title.en: On the board: HTTP, HTTPS and a firewall

say.en: With HTTP, the password travels as plain text. An eavesdropper in between can read it.
With HTTPS the same data is encrypted. The eavesdropper sees only gibberish.
A firewall stands between the internet and our network and checks every packet against rules.

narration.en: We compare a plain-text and an encrypted connection, and then put a firewall at the gate.

body.en: A firewall is a network security system, in hardware or software, that monitors incoming and outgoing traffic and allows or blocks it according to predefined security rules. A network firewall protects a whole network at its gateway; a host-based (software) firewall protects one computer. Cookies are small text files that a website stores in the browser to remember the user, for example a login, language choice or shopping cart. Cookies are not programs and cannot run, but third-party cookies can be used to track a user across many sites, which is a privacy concern; browsers let users block or delete them.

points.en: Firewall: filters traffic by rules (network or host-based)
Cookies: small text files that remember the user
Third-party cookies can track you; clear or block them

narration.kn: ಫೈರ್‌ವಾಲ್ ನಿಯಮಗಳ ಆಧಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ಜಾಲ ಸಂಚಾರವನ್ನು ಅನುಮತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಅಥವಾ ತಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಕುಕೀಗಳು ಬಳಕೆದಾರರನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಡಲು ಬ್ರೌಸರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಇಡುವ ಸಣ್ಣ ಪಠ್ಯ ಕಡತಗಳು; ಮೂರನೇ ಪಕ್ಷದ ಕುಕೀಗಳು ಹಿಂಬಾಲಿಸಬಹುದು.

caption.en: Data crosses the internet as packets that pass through many routers. Over plain HTTP, any of these hops could read a packet; HTTPS keeps the contents encrypted.

tryThis.en: Count how many routers one packet passes through.
Imagine one router is controlled by an attacker: what can it read over HTTP, and over HTTPS?

problem.en: For each situation say whether it is safe and why: (a) Entering card details on http://shop-deals.example (no padlock). (b) Logging in to https://netbanking of your bank with the padlock shown. (c) Clicking "Accept all cookies" on every website you visit.

steps.en: (a) Unsafe: HTTP sends the card number as plain text, readable if intercepted
(b) Safer: HTTPS encrypts the login data in transit (still check the address is the real bank)
(c) Privacy risk: third-party cookies may track you across sites; accept only necessary cookies and clear them regularly

answer.en: (a) Unsafe  (b) Safe in transit  (c) Privacy risk

narration.en: Look for the padlock and https, and be choosy about cookies.
